q: An anaesthetist sustains a deep needlestick injury from a patient known to be HIV-positive with an unknown viral load. After encouraging bleeding and washing, what is the next step?
o: Take no action if the patient is on antiretrovirals
Arrange a hepatitis B booster only
Report immediately to occupational health or the emergency department so that HIV post-exposure prophylaxis can be started as soon as possible, ideally within an hour
Wait for the patient's viral load before deciding
why: PEP should be started as soon as possible, ideally within an hour and no later than 72 hours, continued for 28 days. If the source has a confirmed undetectable viral load on treatment, PEP may not be needed (decided by the specialist). Approximate transmission risks after percutaneous exposure: HBV (HBeAg-positive) up to 30%, HCV about 1.8% (lower in recent data), HIV about 0.3%. Test the source (with consent) and follow up.

q: A patient on antiretroviral therapy including ritonavir is having surgery. Which interaction is most important?
o: Ritonavir has no interactions with anaesthetic drugs
Ritonavir induces CYP3A4, reducing midazolam effect
Ritonavir strongly inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the effect of midazolam, fentanyl and other CYP3A4 substrates
why: Protease inhibitor boosters (ritonavir, cobicistat) are potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, raising levels of midazolam (prolonged sedation; avoid or reduce), fentanyl and alfentanil, and some local anaesthetics. Efavirenz induces enzymes. Check interactions (Liverpool HIV drug interactions database) and do not interrupt therapy.

q: Which protection is required for staff during an aerosol-generating procedure on a patient with a confirmed airborne respiratory infection?
o: Surgical mask and visor without gown
FFP3 respirator (fit-tested), eye protection, long-sleeved gown and gloves
No PPE if the procedure is short
why: For AGPs (e.g. intubation, extubation, NIV, high-flow nasal oxygen, bronchoscopy, tracheostomy) in patients with infections spread by aerosol, staff need airborne precautions: a fit-tested FFP3 respirator, eye protection, fluid-resistant gown and gloves, a minimum number of staff, and adequate air changes. Droplet precautions use a fluid-resistant surgical mask.
